PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,                            §               ADMINISTRATIVE
CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,                            §
MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS,                            §                   HEARINGS
SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                            §
AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                     §



                                           JOHN M. BURROW’S

                 MOTION FOR CLARIFICATION OF SOAH ORDER NO. 25



        John Burrow, a pro se intervenor, respectfully and timely files this request that the State

Office of Administrative Hearings ("SOAH") Administrative Law Judges ("ALJs") provide

clarification to the ALJs ruling to deny Mr. Burrow’s request for remedy and relief due to lack of

proper landowner notification.




Burrow 59475 – Motion for clarification                                                    Page 1 of 4
                                            I. INTRODUCTION

A. John M. Burrow (“Mr. Burrow”), pro se Intervenor in 59475 here provides his MOTION

    FOR CLARIFICATION to the Honorable ALJ’s ruling in SOAH ORDER 25.

B. The pleading at issue in this clarification request is Mr. Burrow’s Motion for Immediate

    Remedy and Relief Due to Applicants Failure to Provide Required Notice (59475-5123).

C. In response to the above pleading, the Honorable ALJs’ ruling briefly restated Mr. Burrow’s

    arguments and then stated only, “This matter is subject to the 180-day deadline of Public

    Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) section 37.057, so extension of the procedural schedule is not

    feasible. Mr. Burrow also did not identify any statute or rule regarding notice that Applicants

    failed to comply with. The motion of Mr. Burrow and 176 aligned landowners is DENIED.”

D. At pages 3-4 of Order 25, the ALJs dismisses the non-notified landowners by denying the

    motion for remedy and relief.



                                          II. LEGAL ARGUMENT

A. The Texas APA at Texas Gov’t Code § 2001.051(2) provides that Mr. Burrow, an Intervenor

    and thereby a “party” to this contested case, is “entitled to an opportunity…to respond and to

    present evidence and argument on each issue involved in the case.”.

B. The Applicants have now divulged in their response to Anna Thorton’s RFI (59475-5768)

    that they did not obtain current county tax rolls, as required by 16 Tex. Admin. Code

    22.52.(a).(3) and as correctly asserted by Mr. Burrow in his motion for remedy and relief.

C. Mr. Burrow asserts that each of the now known twenty-seven (27) landowners and all

    unknown landowners, not notified and who were denied remedy and relief in Order 25, are

    similarly entitled under § 2001.051(2). A notice of default has not been served on them, and

    so they remain “parties” in this contested case, though some may be non-notified parties, not

    yet provided due notice and opportunity to intervene.

Burrow 59475 – Motion for clarification                                                  Page 2 of 4
 D. Mr. Burrow respectfully observes that the ALJs’ ruling “This matter is subject to the 180-day

    deadline of Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA) section 37.057, so extension of the

    procedural schedule is not feasible. Mr. Burrow also did not identify any statute or rule

    regarding notice that Applicants failed to comply with. The motion of Mr. Burrow and 176

    aligned landowners is DENIED.” is ambiguous and fails to state a reasoned basis.

E. Mr. Burrow argued PURA section 37.057 was not in conflict with 16 Tex. Admin. Code

    22.52.(a) and he cited multiple rules regarding notice with which the Applicants failed to

    comply, so he cannot ascertain whether his motion was overruled and denied on procedural

    grounds, jurisdictional grounds, on the substantive merits or any other reasoned basis. The

    ruling failed to state any findings or conclusions, and it is without any legal reasoning. The

    ruling thereby makes it impossible for Mr. Burrow and non-notified landowners to respond to

    and argue the issue(s), as allowed in 2001.051(2), identified by the ALJs because no true

    issue was identified by them in the ruling.

E. The ambiguity of Order 25 has created a review defect in violation of due course of law and

    due process provisions of the Texas and U.S. Constitutions. Texas Constitution, Tex. Const.

    art. I, § 19, the U.S. Constitution, U.S. Const. Amend XIV, § 1. This ambiguity has already

    prevented Mr. Burrow and non-notified landowners from raising any specific issue on appeal

    to the PUC Commissioners and will prevent them from raising any specific issue on appeal to

    a Travis County District Court under the Texas APA at § 2001.174.




Burrow 59475 – Motion for clarification                                                    Page 3 of 4
                                    III. CLARIFICATION REQUESTED

        Mr. Burrow respectfully requests that the ALJs authoring Order 25 identify their

reasoned basis for denying his motion and deferring to PURA section 37.057. Mr. Burrow also

requests other and further relief to which he may be entitled.




Date Signed: June 4, 2026


Respectfully submitted,

John M. Burrow
